$comment: Default deterministic PT-EN IT jargon substitutions (SPEC.md FR-9, US-2). 'from' is a measured or expected ASR misrendering, 'to' is the canonical spelling. Matching is word-boundary anchored and case/diacritic-insensitive, so 'comite' also covers 'comitê' and no entry can match inside a longer word. User-editable: copy this file and load it with JargonDictionary.load(contentsOf:).
$safety: 'safety' decides whether an entry is ACTIVE. safe = 'from' is not Brazilian Portuguese, so it cannot overwrite correct text. contextual = 'from' is plausible Portuguese, so it only fires when one of its contextBefore/contextAfter words is within 3 word tokens on that side. risky = 'from' is common Portuguese with no disambiguating context; excluded unless the caller passes includeRisky: true. Never promote an entry to 'safe' without checking that 'from' is not a real Portuguese word.
$provenance: Terms marked 'Spike 0 RUN 1' were produced by FluidAudio 0.15.5 + Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 on the user's own recordings, 2026-08-02. See SPEC.md section 6.

entries.note: Spike 0 RUN 1: 'Docker Compose' -> 'docker com pose'. The three-word form is unambiguous, and longest-match makes it win over 'com pose'.
Spike 0 RUN 1. 'com pose' is legitimate Portuguese ('veio com pose de chefe'), so it needs Docker nearby. Catches renderings the three-word entry misses, e.g. 'o docker, com pose'.
Spike 0 RUN 1: 'Postgres' -> 'posterg'. A fragment, never a standalone Portuguese word; 'postergar' is a different token and cannot match.
Spike 0 RUN 1: 'branch' -> 'brand'. Not a Portuguese word. Cost of a wrong fire is low: both readings are English and the user sees it.
Spike 0 RUN 1: 'staging' -> 'station'. Not a Portuguese word (that would be 'estação').
Spike 0 RUN 1: 'commit' -> 'comite'. Folding makes this also match 'comitê', which is a real Portuguese word (committee) — hence contextual, never safe.
Plural of the entry above; 'comitês' folds onto it.

Spike 0 RUN 1, Audio_1: 'deploy' -> 'depois'. DISABLED ON PURPOSE. 'depois' is among the most common words in Portuguese, and the same fixture sentence ('Fazer deploy ... depois do merge') contains a correct 'depois', so any unconditional rule fixes one word and breaks the other. No local context separates the readings. The real fix is engine-side: vocabulary biasing via JargonDictionary.biasTerms, or the WhisperKit fallback of NFR-2.
Spike 0 RUN 1, Audio_1: 'merge' -> 'me'. DISABLED ON PURPOSE. 'me' is a Portuguese clitic pronoun ('ele me disse'). Same reasoning as 'depois'.
